On this page Copy page ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/board-pic.png) Introduction[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#introduction "Direct link to Introduction") ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- **Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C3** is an IoT mini development board based on the Espressif **ESP32-C3** WiFi/Bluetooth dual-mode chip, featuring a **32-bit RISC-V CPU** that delivers powerful computing performance with its efficient architecture. It has excellent radio frequency performance, supporting **IEEE 802.11 b/g/n WiFi**, and **Bluetooth 5 (BLE)** protocols. This board comes included with an external antenna to increase the signal strength for your wireless applications. It also has a **small and exquisite form-factor** combined with a **single-sided surface-mountable design**. It is equipped with rich interfaces and has **11 digital I/O** that can be used as **PWM pins** and **4 analog I/O** that can be used as **ADC pins**. It supports four serial interfaces such as **UART, I2C and SPI**. There is also a small **reset button** and a **bootloader mode button** on the board. XIAO ESP32C3 is fully compatible with the [Grove Shield for Seeeduino XIAO](https://www.seeedstudio.com/Grove-Shield-for-Seeeduino-XIAO-p-4621.html) and [Seeeduino XIAO Expansion board](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/Seeeduino-XIAO-Expansion-Board) except for the Seeeduino XIAO Expansion board, the SWD spring contacts on the board will not be compatible. With regard to the features highlighted above, XIAO ESP32C3 is positioned as a **high-performance, low-power, cost-effective IoT mini development board**, suitable for **low-power IoT applications and wireless wearable applications**. This wiki will show you how you can quickly get started with XIAO ESP32C3! [**Get One Now 🖱️**](https://www.seeedstudio.com/seeed-xiao-esp32c3-p-5431.html) ### Specifications[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#specifications "Direct link to Specifications") | Parameter | Description | | --- | --- | | Processor | ESP32-C3 SoC

Light-sleep Mode: 10 mA | | Working Temperature | \-40°C ~ 85°C | ### Features[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#features "Direct link to Features") * **Powerful CPU:** ESP32-C3, 32­bit RISC­-V single­core processor that operates at up to 160 MHz * **Complete Wi­Fi subsystem:** Complies with IEEE 802.11b/g/n protocol and supports Station mode, SoftAP mode, SoftAP + Station mode, and promiscuous mode * **Bluetooth LE subsystem:** Supports features of Bluetooth 5 and Bluetooth mesh * **Ultra-Low Power:** Deep sleep power consumption is about 43μA * **Better RF performance:** External RF antenna included * **Battery charging chip:** Supports lithium battery charge and discharge management * **Rich on-chip resources:** 400KB of SRAM, and 4MB of on-board flash memory * **Ultra small size:** As small as a thumb(21x17.8mm) XIAO series classic form-factor for wearable devices and small projects * **Reliable security features:** Cryptographic hardware accelerators that support AES-128/256, Hash, RSA, HMAC, digital signature and secure boot * **Rich interfaces:** 1xI2C, 1xSPI, 2xUART, 11xGPIO(PWM), 4xADC, 1xJTAG bonding pad interface * Single-sided components, surface mounting design Hardware overview[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#hardware-overview "Direct link to Hardware overview") -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- > \*A3(GP105) - Uses ADC2, which may become inoperative due to false sampling signals. For reliable analog reads, use ADC1(A0/A1/A2) instead. Refer to the ESP32-C3 datasheet. ### Front[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#front "Direct link to Front") ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/XIAO_ESP32-C3_front_pinout.png) ### Back[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#back "Direct link to Back") ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/XIAO_ESP32-C3_back_pinout.png) Pin Map[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#pin-map "Direct link to Pin Map") -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | XIAO Pin | Function | Chip Pin | Alternate Functions | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 5V | VBUS | | | Power Input/Output | | GND | | | | | | 3V3 | 3V3\_OUT | | | Power Output | | D0 | Analog | GPIO2 | ADC1\_CH2, | GPIO, ADC | | D1 | Analog | GPIO3 | ADC1\_CH3 | GPIO, ADC | | D2 | Analog | GPIO4 | ADC1\_CH4, FSPIHD, MTMS | GPIO, ADC | | D3 | Analog | GPIO5 | ADC2\_CH0, FSPIWP, MTDI | GPIO, ADC | | D4 | SDA | GPIO6 | FSPICLK, MTCK | GPIO, I2C Data | | D5 | SCL | GPIO7 | FSPID, MTDO | GPIO, I2C Clock | | D6 | TX | GPIO21 | U0TXD | GPIO, UART Transmit | | D7 | RX | GPIO20 | U0RXD | GPIO, UART Receive | | D8 | SCK | GPIO8 | | GPIO, SPI Clock | | D9 | MISO | GPIO9 | | GPIO, SPI Data | | D10 | MOSI | GPIO10 | FSPICS0 | GPIO, SPI Data | | MTDO | | GPIO7 | | JTAG | | MTDI | | GPIO5 | | JTAG, ADC | | MTCK | | GPIO6 | | JTAG, ADC | | MTMS | | GPIO4 | | JTAG, ADC | | Reset | | CHIP\_EN | | EN | | Boot | | GPIO9 | | Enter Boot Mode | | U.FL-R-SMT1 | | LNA\_IN | | UFL antenna | | Light | | VCC\_3V3 | | CHG-LED | ### Power Pins[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#power-pins "Direct link to Power Pins") * 5V - This is 5v out from the USB port. You can also use this as a voltage input but you must have some sort of diode (schottky, signal, power) between your external power source and this pin with anode to battery, cathode to 5V pin. * 3V3 - This is the regulated output from the onboard regulator. You can draw 700mA * GND - Power/data/signal ground ### Strapping Pins[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#strapping-pins "Direct link to Strapping Pins") According to the chip manual of ESP32C3, **GPIO2**, **GPIO8** and **GPIO9** in the chip are Strapping Pins, the high and low level configurations of these pins may allow the chip to enter into different Boot modes, please pay attention to this point when you use these pins, otherwise it may prevent your XIAO from uploading or executing the program all the time. ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/20.png) Getting started[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#getting-started "Direct link to Getting started") -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- First, we are going to connect XIAO ESP32C3 to the computer, connect an LED to the board and upload a simple code from Arduino IDE to check whether the board is functioning well by blinking the connected LED. ### Hardware Preparation[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#hardware-preparation "Direct link to Hardware Preparation") You need to prepare the following: * 1 x [Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C3](https://www.seeedstudio.com/seeed-xiao-esp32c3-p-5431.html) * 1 x Computer * 1 x USB Type-C cable tip Some USB cables can only supply power and cannot transfer data. If you don't have a USB cable or don't know if your USB cable can transmit data, you can check [Seeed USB Type-C support USB 3.1](https://www.seeedstudio.com/USB-3-1-Type-C-to-A-Cable-1-Meter-3-1A-p-4085.html) . * **Step 1.** Connect XIAO ESP32C3 to your computer via a USB Type-C cable. ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/cable-connect.png) * **Step 2.** Connect an LED to D10 pin as follows ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/connect-led-2.png) **Note:** Make sure to connect a resistor (about 150Ω) in series to limit the current through the LED and to prevent excess current that can burn out the LED ### Software Preparation[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#software-preparation "Direct link to Software Preparation") * **Step 1.** Download and Install the latest version of Arduino IDE according to your operating system [![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/Seeeduino_Stalker_V3_1/images/Download_IDE.png)](https://www.arduino.cc/en/software) * **Step 2.** Launch the Arduino application * **Step 3.** Add ESP32 board package to your Arduino IDE Navigate to **File > Preferences**, and fill **"Additional Boards Manager URLs"** with the url below: _[https://jihulab.com/esp-mirror/espressif/arduino-esp32.git](https://jihulab.com/esp-mirror/espressif/arduino-esp32.git) _ ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/add_board.png) Navigate to **Tools > Board > Boards Manager...**, type the keyword "**esp32**" in the search box, select the latest version of **esp32**, and install it. ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/add_esp32c3.png) * **Step 4.** Select your board and port **Board** Navigate to **Tools > Board > ESP32 Arduino** and select "**XIAO\_ESP32C3**". The list of board is a little long and you need to roll to the buttom to reach it. ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/Seeed-Studio-XIAO-ESP32/XIAO_ESP32_board.png) **Port** Navigate to **Tools > Port** and select the serial port name of the connected XIAO ESP32C3. This is likely to be COM3 or higher (**COM1** and **COM2** are usually reserved for hardware serial ports). ### Run your first Blink program[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#run-your-first-blink-program "Direct link to Run your first Blink program") * **Step 1.** Copy the below code to Arduino IDE Make sure your `D10` is connected to an LED as shown in the diagram above. // define led according to pin diagram in articleconst int led = D10; // there is no LED_BUILTIN available for the XIAO ESP32C3.void setup() { // initialize digital pin led as an output pinMode(led, OUTPUT);}void loop() { digitalWrite(led, HIGH); // turn the LED on delay(1000); // wait for a second digitalWrite(led, LOW); // turn the LED off delay(1000); // wait for a second} * **Step 2.** Click the **Upload** button to upload the code to the board ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/Seeeduino_GPRS/img/upload_image.png) Once uploaded, you will see the connected LED blinking with a 1-second delay between each blink. This means the connection is successful and now you can explore more projects with XIAO ESP32C3! Battery Usage[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#battery-usage "Direct link to Battery Usage") -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The XIAO ESP32C3 is capable of using a 3.7V lithium battery as the power supply input. You can refer to the following diagram for the wiring method. ![pir](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/battery_connect.png) caution Please be careful not to short-circuit the positive and negative terminals and burn the battery and equipment when soldering. **Instructions on the use of batteries:** 1. Please use qualified batteries that meet the specifications. 2. XIAO can be connected to your computer device via data cable while using the battery, rest assured that XIAO has a built-in circuit protection chip, which is safe. 3. The XIAO ESP32C3 will not have any LED on when it is battery powered (unless you have written a specific program), please do not judge whether the XIAO ESP32C3 is working or not by the condition of the LED, please judge it reasonably by your program. 4. Sorry, we currently have no way to help you check the remaining battery level through software (because there are no more chip pins available), you need to charge the battery regularly or use a multimeter to check the battery level. ### Check the battery voltage[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#check-the-battery-voltage "Direct link to Check the battery voltage") Due to the limitation of the number of pins in the ESP32C3, engineers had no extra pins to allocate to the battery for voltage measurement in order to ensure that the XIAO ESP32C3 has the same number of GPIOs as the other XIAO series available. But if you prefer to use a separate pin for battery voltage measurement, you can refer to the genius operation of [msfujino](https://forum.seeedstudio.com/u/msfujino) . We would also like to give a special thanks to [msfujino](https://forum.seeedstudio.com/u/msfujino) for all the experience and efforts shared for the XIAO ESP32C3. The basic operating idea is: The battery voltage was divided by 1/2 with 200k and connected to the A0 port so that the voltage could be monitored. ![pir](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/3.png) The datasheet says nominally 2500mV full scale AD conversion, but there is a large variation from chip to chip, actually ±10%. My chip was 2700mV full scale. Fortunately, the calibrated correction value for each chip is written in the fuse area, and by using the function `analogReadMilliVolts()`, I can read the corrected voltage value without doing anything special. The result of AD conversion and the voltage measured by the multimeter agree well with each other with an error of about 5 mV, which is not a problem in practical use. In addition, during communication in particular, spike-like errors occurred, which had to be averaged out 16 times to remove them. The following is the procedure to test the battery voltage. void setup() { Serial.begin(115200); pinMode(A0, INPUT); // ADC}void loop() { uint32_t Vbatt = 0; for(int i = 0; i < 16; i++) { Vbatt = Vbatt + analogReadMilliVolts(A0); // ADC with correction } float Vbattf = 2 * Vbatt / 16 / 1000.0; // attenuation ratio 1/2, mV --> V Serial.println(Vbattf, 3); delay(1000);} tip The above is from Seeed Studio forum user **msfujino**, originally posted at: [https://forum.seeedstudio.com/t/battery-voltage-monitor-and-ad-conversion-for-xiao-esp32c/267535](https://forum.seeedstudio.com/t/battery-voltage-monitor-and-ad-conversion-for-xiao-esp32c/267535) . We recommend that you have good hands-on skills and better soldering skills before attempting to measure battery voltage based on the above, and be cautious of dangerous actions such as shorting out batteries. Deep sleep mode and wake-up[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#deep-sleep-mode-and-wake-up "Direct link to Deep sleep mode and wake-up") -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The XIAO ESP32C3 is designed to support deep sleep mode and wake-up functions. For the use of these two functions, we provide the following usage examples. #define BUTTON_PIN_BITMASK 0x200000000 // 2^33 in hexRTC_DATA_ATTR int bootCount = 0;/*Method to print the reason by which ESP32has been awaken from sleep*/void print_wakeup_reason(){ esp_sleep_wakeup_cause_t wakeup_reason; wakeup_reason = esp_sleep_get_wakeup_cause(); switch(wakeup_reason) { case ESP_SLEEP_WAKEUP_EXT0 : Serial.println("Wakeup caused by external signal using RTC_IO"); break; case ESP_SLEEP_WAKEUP_EXT1 : Serial.println("Wakeup caused by external signal using RTC_CNTL"); break; case ESP_SLEEP_WAKEUP_TIMER : Serial.println("Wakeup caused by timer"); break; case ESP_SLEEP_WAKEUP_TOUCHPAD : Serial.println("Wakeup caused by touchpad"); break; case ESP_SLEEP_WAKEUP_ULP : Serial.println("Wakeup caused by ULP program"); break; default : Serial.printf("Wakeup was not caused by deep sleep: %d\n",wakeup_reason); break; }}void setup(){ Serial.begin(115200); delay(1000); //Take some time to open up the Serial Monitor //Increment boot number and print it every reboot ++bootCount; Serial.println("Boot number: " + String(bootCount)); //Print the wakeup reason for ESP32 print_wakeup_reason(); esp_deep_sleep_enable_gpio_wakeup(BIT(D1), ESP_GPIO_WAKEUP_GPIO_LOW); //Go to sleep now Serial.println("Going to sleep now"); esp_deep_sleep_start(); Serial.println("This will never be printed");}void loop(){ //This is not going to be called} If you are quick enough to turn on the serial monitor before the XIAO goes into deep sleep, then you can see the message output as shown below. This means that the XIAO is now "asleep". ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/15.png) tip After entering deep sleep mode, the XIAO's port will disappear and you'll need to wake it up to see its port number again! In the program, we are using a **D1** low level to wake up. This means that we can connect a button to pin D1 and the XIAO will wake up when we press the button. caution The XIAO ESP32-C3 supports GPIO wake-up and timer wake-up, and the pins that support wake-up are D0~D3. Troubleshooting[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#troubleshooting "Direct link to Troubleshooting") -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ### Q1: My Arduino IDE is stuck when uploading code to the board[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#q1-my-arduino-ide-is-stuck-when-uploading-code-to-the-board "Direct link to Q1: My Arduino IDE is stuck when uploading code to the board") You can first try to reset the board by clicking the **RESET BUTTON** once while the board is connected to your PC. If that does not work, hold the **BOOT BUTTON**, connect the board to your PC while holding the **BOOT** button, and then release it to enter **bootloader mode**. ### Q2: My board is not showing up as a serial device on Arduino IDE[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#q2-my-board-is-not-showing-up-as-a-serial-device-on-arduino-ide "Direct link to Q2: My board is not showing up as a serial device on Arduino IDE") Follow the same answer as for **Q1** above. ### Q3: I want to reflash the bootloader with factory firmware[​](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#q3-i-want-to-reflash-the-bootloader-with-factory-firmware "Direct link to Q3: I want to reflash the bootloader with factory firmware") You can simply connect the board to a PC via **USB Type-C** and reflash the bootloader with factory firmware by using **ESP RF Test Tool**. * **Step 1.** Hold on the **BOOT BUTTON** and page](https://www.espressif.com/en/support/download/other-tools) and download **ESP RF Test Tool and Test Guide** ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/esp-flash-tool-download.png) * **Step 4.** Extract the **.zip**, navigate to `ESP_RF_Test_EN\ESP_RF_Test_EN\EspRFTestTool_v2.8_Manual` and open **EspRFTestTool\_v2.8\_Manual.exe** ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/esp-flash-tool-open.png) * **Step 5.** Select **ESP32C3** as the ChipType, your COM port, **115200** as the BaudRate and click **open** ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/esp-flash-2.png) You will see the following output ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/esp-flash-5.png) * **Step 6.** Select **Flash** and ESP32C3](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/Resources/ESP32-C3_RFTest_108_2b9b157_20211014.bin) and select it. * **Step 8.** Finally click **Load Bin** ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/esp-flash-8.png) You will see the following output when flashing is successful ![](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/esp-flash-9.png) The **XIAO ESP32C3 pinout** brings out 14 pins at a 2.54 mm pitch - 11 usable GPIO alongside the `5V`, `GND` and `3V3` power rails.

Peripheral wiring is straightforward: I²C is mapped to `SDA` on GPIO6 and `SCL` on GPIO7; the SPI bus (`MOSI`, `MISO`, `SCK`) is broken out in full; `TX`/`RX` on GPIO21 and GPIO20 cover serial logging and flashing.

Beyond plain digital I/O you get 4 ADC-capable pins for sensors and battery monitoring and PWM on every GPIO.

9 of the exposed pins carry boot-time or system duties on the ESP32-C3 (`D0`, `D2`, `D3` and 6 more) - check the guidance above before wiring anything to them. `D1` and `D10` are free of any such role - the safest first picks.

flash your first firmware in ~2 minutes

Connect over USB

Match & flash

3

Verify it runs

The onboard LED on GPIO3 blinks - swap the pin if your board's LED differs.

Set these in Tools · leave everything else at default

    // blink the onboard LED

Around the module: battery charging, status LEDs (Charge) and Reset/Boot buttons.

It flashes over native USB - no serial-converter driver needed, which isn't a given among ESP32-C3 boards.

*   Low power consumption with deep sleep support
*   Ships with an external u.FL antenna

The ESP32-C3 chip is built around 32-bit RISC-V architecture with four stage pipeline and a Floating-Point Unit (FPU) for precision arithmetic operations. The chip also has 2.4GHz WiFi and Bluetooth 5(LE) support.

Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C3 Guide: Hardware, Battery, Low Power, WiFi and Antenna
================================================================================

by OpenELAB

on Aug 04

Hardware Overview
-----------------

The [Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C3](https://openelab.io/products/seeed-studio-xiao-esp32c3)
 is built around Espressif's ESP32-C3 system-on-chip. Its single-core, 32-bit RISC-V processor runs at up to 160 MHz and is paired with 400 KB of SRAM and 4 MB of onboard flash. That is enough for typical sensor nodes, compact web interfaces, MQTT clients, Bluetooth devices and home-automation endpoints.

Wireless capability is part of the processor rather than an add-on module. The board supports 2.4 GHz IEEE 802.11 b/g/n WiFi as well as Bluetooth 5 Low Energy and Bluetooth Mesh. Seeed routes the radio to a small IPEX/U.FL-style connector and includes an external flexible antenna, which is an important part of the board's wireless design.

![Official product photograph of the Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C3 development board](https://media-cdn.seeedstudio.com/media/catalog/product/1/-/1-113991054-seeed-studio-xiao-esp32c3-45font_1.jpg)

Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C3 with USB-C, RF connector, reset and boot buttons. [View the XIAO ESP32-C3](https://openelab.io/products/seeed-studio-xiao-esp32c3)
.

[View XIAO ESP32-C3](https://openelab.io/products/seeed-studio-xiao-esp32c3)

Despite its small format, the board exposes 11 GPIOs that can be used for digital I/O and PWM, with four analog inputs for ADC measurements. It also provides UART, I2C and SPI interfaces, plus reset and boot buttons. USB-C is used for power and programming. Components are mounted on one side, so the board can be placed on headers, used with XIAO expansion boards or integrated into a compact device.

The ESP32-C3 also includes hardware security functions such as AES-128/256 acceleration, hashing, RSA, HMAC, digital-signature support and secure boot. These features do not secure an application automatically, but they give developers appropriate building blocks for authenticated devices and protected firmware.

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Processor | Espressif ESP32-C3, 32-bit single-core RISC-V, up to 160 MHz |
| Memory | 400 KB SRAM and 4 MB onboard flash |
| Wireless | 2.4 GHz WiFi 802.11 b/g/n; Bluetooth 5 Low Energy; Bluetooth Mesh |
| Interfaces | 11 GPIO/PWM, 4 ADC, UART, I2C, SPI, reset button and boot button |
| Programming and power | USB-C; 5 V VIN; regulated 3.3 V output |
| Battery input | 3.7 V rechargeable lithium battery through underside BAT pads |
| Charging current | Approximately 380 mA fast charge and 40 mA trickle charge |
| Deep sleep | Approximately 44 µA under Seeed's documented test conditions |
| Dimensions | 21 x 17.8 mm |
| Operating temperature | \-40°C to 85°C |

The specifications make the board most attractive when space, wireless connectivity and energy use all matter. It is not intended to replace a high-memory application processor, but it provides a useful balance for embedded IoT work.

Supported Development Ecosystem
-------------------------------

The XIAO ESP32-C3 is not limited to a single programming workflow. Seeed provides board-specific documentation for several common embedded-development environments, while the underlying ESP32-C3 benefits from Espressif's broader software ecosystem.

### Arduino IDE

[Arduino IDE](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#software-preparation)
 is the most direct starting point. After installing the Espressif ESP32 board package, developers can select `XIAO_ESP32C3` as the target and upload sketches through USB-C. This route provides access to the Arduino WiFi, BLE, GPIO and peripheral libraries, making it practical for prototypes and familiar embedded C++ projects.

### PlatformIO

[PlatformIO](https://docs.platformio.org/en/latest/boards/espressif32/seeed_xiao_esp32c3.html)
 provides a more structured workflow inside Visual Studio Code and other supported editors. The board ID is `seeed_xiao_esp32c3`. PlatformIO lists both the Arduino framework and Espressif IoT Development Framework as supported options, so developers can keep project dependencies and build settings in version-controlled configuration files.

### Espressif ESP-IDF

For lower-level control, production firmware and direct access to Espressif APIs, the board can be developed with [ESP-IDF](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_idf/)
 by setting the target to `esp32c3`. ESP-IDF exposes the chip's networking stack, FreeRTOS-based task model, sleep APIs, security functions and detailed radio configuration. It has a steeper learning curve than Arduino, but it gives experienced developers more control over memory, scheduling and power behavior.

### MicroPython

Seeed also documents [MicroPython workflows for the XIAO ESP32-C3](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_esp32c3_with_micropython/)
. A compatible ESP32-C3 firmware can be flashed to the board and used from tools such as Thonny. MicroPython is useful for education, quick hardware experiments and applications where iteration speed matters more than the smallest possible firmware footprint.

### ESPHome and Home Assistant

For smart-home projects, Seeed provides an [ESPHome guide for connecting the board](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO-ESP32C3-for-ESPHome-Support/)
 to [Home Assistant](https://www.home-assistant.io/)
. ESPHome turns YAML configuration into firmware and supports local sensor reporting, switches, automations and over-the-air updates. This makes the XIAO ESP32-C3 suitable for compact WiFi sensor nodes without requiring every feature to be written from scratch.

**Choosing a workflow:** Arduino is usually the fastest route to a working prototype; PlatformIO adds stronger project organization; ESP-IDF offers the deepest control; MicroPython favors rapid experimentation; and ESPHome is purpose-built for Home Assistant devices.

XIAO ESP32C3 Battery and Low-Power Operation
--------------------------------------------

The board can run from a 3.7 V rechargeable lithium battery connected to the BAT pads on its underside. Its onboard charging circuit allows the battery to charge while USB-C power is connected, with a documented charging current of about 380 mA during fast charge and 40 mA during trickle charge. This integrated function is one reason the board works well in portable sensors and small connected devices.

![Official diagram showing a 3.7 volt lithium battery connected to the BAT pads on the back of the XIAO ESP32-C3](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/XIAO_WiFi/battery_connect.png)

Official XIAO ESP32C3 battery connection diagram. Source: [Seeed Studio Wiki](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#battery-usage)
.

**Battery safety:** Use a qualified 3.7 V rechargeable lithium battery, verify polarity before soldering and never short the BAT pads. The BAT input is not intended for a 5 V, 9 V or 12 V battery source.

The official power figures show why firmware design matters:

| Operating state | Documented typical current |
| --- | --- |
| WiFi active | 75 mA |
| WiFi modem sleep | 25 mA |
| WiFi light sleep | 4 mA |
| BLE modem sleep | 27 mA |
| BLE light sleep | 10 mA |
| Deep sleep | 44 µA |

These values are reference measurements rather than a guaranteed battery-life calculation. Real consumption changes with signal strength, transmit duration, connected sensors, regulator losses, firmware and battery condition. WiFi current can also rise in short bursts during association and transmission, so a battery must handle more than the average current alone suggests.

### Designing for Longer Battery Life

The most effective strategy is duty cycling. A remote sensor can wake on a timer, take a reading, connect to the network, send a compact update and return to deep sleep. In that pattern, the duration and frequency of WiFi activity often matter more than the sleeping current.

*   Keep network sessions short and avoid scanning when known credentials can be reused.
*   Send several readings in one transaction instead of opening a connection for each value.
*   Power down external sensors or displays when their outputs are not needed.
*   Use deep sleep for long idle periods and timer or GPIO wake-up only when the application needs it.
*   Measure the complete assembled device, not only the development board.

One limitation is battery monitoring. The board does not dedicate an internal ADC channel to the BAT voltage, so firmware cannot directly report the remaining battery level. Seeed [documents an external resistor-divider method](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_Getting_Started/#check-the-battery-voltage)
 connected to an analog input for projects that need voltage measurement, but that circuit must be designed with its own standby consumption in mind.

XIAO ESP32C3 WiFi and External Antenna
--------------------------------------

[XIAO ESP32C3 WiFi](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO_ESP32C3_WiFi_Usage/)
 operates on 2.4 GHz networks using IEEE 802.11 b/g/n. The radio supports Station mode for joining an existing router, SoftAP mode for creating a local access point, simultaneous SoftAP and Station operation, and promiscuous mode for specialized network applications.

Station mode is the normal choice for MQTT nodes, local web clients, cloud-connected sensors and Home Assistant devices. SoftAP mode is useful for provisioning, because a phone or computer can connect directly to the device before normal network credentials are stored. Seeed warns that prolonged access-point operation can make the board hot, so SoftAP should be used with suitable operating time, enclosure design and handling precautions.

![Official product photograph showing the flexible external antenna connected to the XIAO ESP32-C3](https://media-cdn.seeedstudio.com/media/catalog/product/5/-/5-113991054-seeed-studio-xiao-esp32c3-feature_1.jpg)

The included flexible 2.4 GHz antenna connected to the board's IPEX RF connector. [View the XIAO ESP32-C3](https://openelab.io/products/seeed-studio-xiao-esp32c3)
.

### Why the External Antenna Matters

The XIAO ESP32C3 antenna is external rather than being etched onto the small board. This gives the radiating element more usable area and lets developers position it away from the processor, battery and other parts of the enclosure. The same antenna path is used for WiFi and Bluetooth.

The included antenna should be connected carefully to the IPEX socket before wireless testing. Press straight down over the connector instead of applying force at an angle. The connector is small and is intended for careful installation rather than frequent disconnection.

Final antenna placement has a direct effect on both reliability and energy use:

*   Keep the flat antenna area away from large batteries, ground planes and metal enclosure walls.
*   Do not fold the radiating section tightly or trap it beneath the board.
*   Test RSSI and connection time with the complete enclosure, battery and wiring installed.
*   Check performance in the actual deployment location rather than relying only on desk testing.

A weak connection is also a low-power problem. When the signal is poor, the device can spend longer associating with the router, repeat transmissions or remain awake while waiting for network responses. Good antenna placement can therefore improve connection stability and shorten the radio-on period that dominates many battery-powered workloads.

Where the XIAO ESP32-C3 Fits Best
---------------------------------

The XIAO ESP32-C3 is a practical option for compact wireless sensors, portable monitors, smart-home endpoints, wearable prototypes and other devices that periodically exchange small amounts of data. Its hardware is capable enough for common IoT workloads, while Arduino, PlatformIO, ESP-IDF, MicroPython and ESPHome give developers several ways to move from a quick experiment to more structured firmware.

Its strongest design combination is the relationship between low-power firmware and the external antenna. Deep sleep can reduce idle current to tens of microamps, but real battery life still depends on how quickly the device can establish a reliable WiFi connection and return to sleep. Treating battery behavior and antenna placement as one system is the best way to get useful results from this small board.

XIAO Series Accessories
-----------------------

The shared XIAO form factor makes it possible to extend the XIAO ESP32-C3 without moving immediately to a custom carrier board. The following accessories are useful when a project needs positioning, additional peripherals or CAN Bus communication.

### L76K GNSS Module for XIAO

L76K GNSS Module with the included active antenna. Official image: [Seeed Studio L76K GNSS tutorial](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/get_start_l76k_gnss/)
.

 covers installation, Arduino setup and basic positioning examples.

Expansion Board Base for XIAO with its onboard display and peripheral connectors. Official image: [Seeed Studio Expansion Board guide](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/Seeeduino-XIAO-Expansion-Board/)

![](https://www.seeed.cc/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.seeed.cc%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F06%2Fwechatimg291-6.jpg&w=1200&q=100) ![](https://www.seeed.cc/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.seeed.cc%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F06%2F5-113991254-seeedxiao-esp32c6-feature_1-6.jpg&w=1200&q=100) ![](https://www.seeed.cc/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.seeed.cc%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F06%2Fwechatimg289-6.jpg&w=1200&q=100) ![](https://www.seeed.cc/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.seeed.cc%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F06%2F1-113991054-seeed-studio-xiao-esp32c3-45font_1-7.jpg&w=1200&q=100) ![](https://www.seeed.cc/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.seeed.cc%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F06%2F113991254-seeed-studio-xiao-esp32c6-6.jpg&w=1200&q=100) XIAO Series Module ================== Compact ESP32-based development boards supporting Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and advanced features for IoT applications and smart home projects * Enhanced Connectivity Multiple wireless protocols including Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.0, Zigbee, and Thread for comprehensive IoT solutions * Matter Native Support Built-in Matter compliance for seamless smart home interoperability and future-proof applications * Security Encrypted on Chip Advanced security features including secure boot, encryption, and Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) * Outstanding RF Performance Up to 100m+ communication range with on-board antenna and external UFL antenna support * Ultra-Low Power Design Multiple power modes with deep sleep as low as 14-44 μA, perfect for battery-powered applications * Thumb-sized Form Factor Classic XIAO 21 x 17.8mm design with single-sided mounting for space-limited wearable projects Request Quote or Consultation Description Specification Wiki & Learn Related Products The Seeed Studio XIAO series represents the latest evolution in compact microcontroller development, offering three powerful variants: ESP32-C6, ESP32-S3 Sense, and ESP32-C3. Each board maintains the classic XIAO form factor while delivering unique capabilities for diverse IoT applications. Enhanced Connectivity and Matter Support The XIAO ESP32-C6 stands out with its comprehensive wireless connectivity, combining 2.4GHz Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax), Bluetooth 5.0, and IEEE 802.15.4 radio connectivity for Thread and Zigbee protocols. This enhanced connectivity makes it natively compatible with Matter-compliant smart home projects, ensuring seamless interoperability across different platforms and devices. Advanced Processing Power The series features different processor architectures optimized for specific use cases. The ESP32-C6 incorporates dual 32-bit RISC-V processors with the high-performance core running up to 160 MHz and a low-power core clocking up to 20 MHz. The ESP32-S3 utilizes an Xtensa LX7 dual-core, 32-bit processor running up to 240 MHz, while the ESP32-C3 features a RISC-V single-core 32-bit processor with four-stage pipeline operating at up to 160 MHz. Memory and Storage Options Memory configurations vary across the series to meet different application requirements. The ESP32-C6 offers 512KB SRAM and 4MB Flash, the ESP32-C3 provides 400KB SRAM and 4MB Flash, while the ESP32-S3 Sense features the most generous 8MB PSRAM and 8MB Flash, with additional SD card slot support for up to 32GB FAT storage. Specialized Features The ESP32-S3 Sense variant includes advanced sensing capabilities with a detachable OV2640 camera sensor supporting 1600x1200 resolution (compatible with OV5640), integrated digital microphone, and pre-trained AI models from SenseCraft AI for no-code deployment. This makes it ideal for embedded machine learning applications including intelligent voice and vision AI projects. Power Management All variants feature sophisticated power management with multiple operating modes. Deep sleep power consumption ranges from 14-44 μA depending on the model, while supporting lithium battery charge management with 100mA charging current. The boards operate from 5V via USB Type-C or 4.2V via battery input. Development Ecosystem The XIAO series integrates seamlessly with the Grove ecosystem through compatible expansion boards, providing access to over 400 Grove modules. Free courses and starter kits are available for beginners, while advanced users can leverage Arduino, MicroPython, and CircuitPython support. The series also supports major IoT cloud platforms including ESP Rain Maker, AWS IoT, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. Production-Ready Design All XIAO ESP32 boards feature production-optimized SMD design with standardized stamp holes, making them perfect for commercial PCBA integration. Through the Fusion PCBA Sponsorship program, users can access lowest unit prices and fabricate XIAO-based designs at reduced cost with free Design for Manufacturing consulting services. 3.Functional Description
This chapter describes the functions of ESP32-C3.
3.1CPU and Memory
3.1.1CPU
ESP32-C3 has a low-power 32-bit RISC-V single-core microprocessor with the following features:
•four-stage pipeline that supports a clock frequency of up to 160 MHz
•RV32IMC ISA
•32-bit multiplier and 32-bit divider
•up to 32 vectored interrupts at seven priority levels
•up to 8 hardware breakpoints/watchpoints
•up to 16 PMP regions
•JTAG for debugging
3.1.2Internal Memory
ESP32-C3’s internal memory includes:

ESP32-C3 supports SPI, Dual SPI, Quad SPI, and QPI interfaces that allow connection to multiple external
flash.
CPU’s instruction memory space and read-only data memory space can map into external flash of ESP32-C3,

3.2System Clocks
3.2.1CPU Clock
The CPU clock has three possible sources:
•external main crystal clock
•fast RC oscillator (typically about 17.5 MHz, and adjustable)
•PLL clock
The application can select the clock source from the three clocks above. The selected clock source drives the
CPU clock directly, or after division, depending on the application. Once the CPU is reset, the default clock
source would be the external main crystal clock divided by 2.
Note:
ESP32-C3 is unable to operate without an external main crystal clock.
3.2.2RTC Clock
The RTC slow clock is used for RTC counter, RTC watchdog and low-power controller. It has three possible
sources:
•external low-speed (32 kHz) crystal clock
•internal slow RC oscillator (typically about 136 kHz, and adjustable)
•internal fast RC oscillator divided clock (derived from the fast RC oscillator divided by 256)
The RTC fast clock is used for RTC peripherals and sensor controllers. It has two possible sources:
•external main crystal clock divided by 2
•internal fast RC oscillator divide-by-N clock (typically about 17.5 MHz, and adjustable)

ESP32-C3 has a general DMA controller (GDMA) with six independent channels, i.e. three transmit channels and
three receive channels. These six channels are shared by peripherals with DMA feature. The GDMA controller
implements a fixed-priority scheme among these channels, whose priority can be configured.
The GDMA controller controls data transfer using linked lists. It allows peripheral-to-memory and
memory-to-memory data transfer at a high speed. All channels can access internal RAM.
Peripherals on ESP32-C3 with DMA feature are SPI2, UHCI0, I2S, AES, SHA, and ADC.

3.7Low Power Management
With the use of advanced power-management technologies, ESP32-C3 can switch between different power
modes.
•Active mode: CPU and chip radio are powered on. The chip can receive, transmit, or listen.
•Modem-sleep mode: The CPU is operational and the clock speed can be reduced. Wi-Fi base band,
Bluetooth LE base band, and radio are disabled, but Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE connection can remain active.
•Light-sleep mode: The CPU is paused. Any wake-up events (MAC, host, RTC timer, or external interrupts)
will wake up the chip. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE connection can remain active.
•Deep-sleep mode: CPU and most peripherals are powered down. Only the RTC memory is powered on.
Wi-Fi connection data are stored in the RTC memory. The RTC timer or the RTC GPIOs can wake up the
chip from the Deep-sleep mode.

3.8.3Watchdog Timers
ESP32-C3 contains three watchdog timers: one in each of the two timer groups (called Main System Watchdog
Timers, or MWDT) and one in the RTC module (called the RTC Watchdog Timer, or RWDT).
During the flash boot process, RWDT and the MWDT in timer group 0 (TIMG0) are enabled automatically in order
to detect and recover from booting errors.
Watchdog timers have the following features:
•four stages, each with a programmable timeout value. Each stage can be configured, enabled and
disabled separately
•interrupt, CPU reset, or core reset for MWDT upon expiry of each stage; interrupt, CPU reset, core reset, or
system reset for RWDT upon expiry of each stage
•32-bit expiry counter
•write protection, to prevent RWDT and MWDT configuration from being altered inadvertently
•flash boot protection
If the boot process from an SPI flash does not complete within a predetermined period of time, the
watchdog will reboot the entire main system.
3.9Cryptographic Hardware Accelerators
ESP32-C3 is equipped with hardware accelerators of general algorithms, such as AES-128/AES-256 (FIPS PUB
197), ECB/CBC/OFB/CFB/CTR (NIST SP 800-38A), SHA1/SHA224/SHA256 (FIPS PUB 180-4), and RSA3072.
The chip also supports independent arithmetic, such as Big Integer Multiplication and Big Integer Modular
Multiplication. The maximum operation length for RSA and Big Integer Modular Multiplication is 3072 bits. The
maximum factor length for Big Integer Multiplication is 1536 bits.
3.10Physical Security Features
•Transparent external flash encryption (AES-XTS algorithm) with software inaccessible key prevents
unauthorized readout of your application code or data.
•Secure boot feature uses a hardware root of trust to ensure only signed firmware (with RSA-PSS signature)
can be booted.
•HMAC module can use a software inaccessible MAC key to generate MAC signatures for identity
verification and other purposes.
•Digital Signature module can use a software inaccessible secure key to generate RSA signatures for identity
verification.
•World Controller provides two running environments for software. All hardware and software resources are
sorted to two groups, and placed in either secure or general world. The secure world cannot be accessed
by hardware in the general world, thus establishing a security boundary.
